aquinas:depot.author: St. Thomas Aquinas
aquinas:depot.locus: Quaestio III, Articulus 11 ('Cum formarum naturalium et corporalium esse non consistat nisi in unione ad materiam...')
aquinas:depot.note: Primary Scholastic epigraph opening the 1917 Cambridge edition, grounding Thompson's thesis that natural physical causes suffice to generate corporeal forms.

archimedes:spirals.author: Archimedes of Syracuse
archimedes:spirals.publisher: Critical ed. J. L. Heiberg (Teubner); English ed. T. L. Heath (Cambridge, 1897)
archimedes:spirals.note: Defines the uniform arithmetic spiral r = aθ, contrasted by Thompson (Ch. XI, pp. 494–498) with the geometric growth law of the equiangular spiral.

aristotle:cat.author: Aristotle
aristotle:cat.note: States that a square, when a gnomon is placed around it, is increased in size (*auxanetai*) without being altered in form (*alloioutai*)—the philosophical kernel of Chapter XI.

aristotle:hist-anim.author: Aristotle
aristotle:hist-anim.locus: Translated by D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson (The Works of Aristotle, Vol. IV)
aristotle:hist-anim.note: Thompson's own landmark English translation of Aristotle's zoology, informing observations on shells, horns, cetaceans, and comparative anatomy across On Growth and Form.

bernoulli:1692.author: Jakob Bernoulli
bernoulli:1692.work: Lineae Cycloidales, Evolutae, Ant-Evolutae, Causticae, Anti-Causticae, Peri-Causticae (Spira Mirabilis)
bernoulli:1692.note: Demonstrates the invariance of the logarithmic spiral under geometric operations and concludes with the motto Eadem mutata resurgo (Ch. XI, p. 504).

boscovich:1760.author: Roger Joseph Boscovich
boscovich:1760.work: Supplement on the Cells of Bees (in Benedict Stay, Philosophiae recentioris versibus traditae libri X, Tom. II)
boscovich:1760.note: Examines Maraldi's honeycomb angle and shows the mathematical sensitivity of the wax minimum around 109° 28′ 16″ (Ch. VII, pp. 332–335).

bravais:1837.author: Louis Bravais & Auguste Bravais
bravais:1837.work: Essai sur la disposition des feuilles curvisériées
bravais:1837.locus: Annales des Sciences Naturelles (Botanique), 2e série, Tome 7, pp. 42–110
bravais:1837.note: Establishes cylindrical lattice geometry and the unique irrational golden divergence angle in spiral phyllotaxis (Ch. XIV).

church:1904.author: Arthur Harry Church
church:1904.work: On the Relation of Phyllotaxis to Mechanical Laws
church:1904.note: Models apical phyllotaxis via orthogonal families of logarithmic spirals; cited both by Thompson (Ch. XIV, pp. 646–650) and by Jay Hambidge (The Diagonal, Vol. I, No. 1, 1919).

culmann:1866.author: Karl Culmann
culmann:1866.note: Foundational treatise of graphic statics whose Fairbairn crane stress trajectories match the cancellous trabeculae of the human femur (Ch. XVI, pp. 679–686).

durer:1528.author: Albrecht Dürer
durer:1528.work: Hierinn sind begriffen vier Bücher von menschlicher Proportion
durer:1528.note: Introduces rectilinear, oblique, and circular coordinate deformations of human heads and bodies, honoured by Thompson (Ch. XVII, pp. 727, 768) as the precursor of transformation grids.

euclid:elements.author: Euclid of Alexandria
euclid:elements.locus: Books II (Def. 2, Prop. 11), IV (Prop. 10), VI (Def. 1 & 3, Prop. 30), X (Def. 1–4), XI, XIII
euclid:elements.note: Classical geometric foundation for gnomons, extreme and mean ratio, the 36°–72°–72° golden triangle, similitude, commensurability in square (dynamis), and the five regular polyhedra.

fidler:1887.author: Thomas Claxton Fidler
fidler:1887.work: A Practical Treatise on Bridge-Construction: Being a Text-Book on the Design and Construction of Bridges in Iron and Steel
fidler:1887.note: Source of the cantilever and Forth-Bridge reciprocal stress frameworks applied by Thompson to vertebrate skeletons and dinosaur spines in Chapter XVI (pp. 694–712).

galileo:1638.author: Galileo Galilei
galileo:1638.work: Discorsi e Dimostrazioni Matematiche, intorno à due nuove scienze
galileo:1638.locus: Giornata Seconda (Strength of Beams & Scaling of Bones)
galileo:1638.note: Formulates the Square-Cube Law governing maximum size of trees, terrestrial quadrupeds, and marine cetaceans (Ch. II, pp. 19–28).

haeckel:1887.author: Ernst Haeckel
haeckel:1887.work: Report on the Radiolaria Collected by H.M.S. Challenger during the Years 1873–1876
haeckel:1887.note: Monumental Challenger monograph whose polyhedral and spicular Radiolaria are analyzed physically via liquid-film geometry in Chapter IX (pp. 468–487).

hambidge:1920-diagonal.author: Jay Hambidge
hambidge:1920-diagonal.work: The Diagonal: An Illustrated Monthly Magazine Devoted to the Explanation of the Rediscovered Principles of Greek Design ('The Elements of Dynamic Symmetry')
hambidge:1920-diagonal.note: Primary public-domain serial source of Hambidge's Elements of Dynamic Symmetry lessons: sunflower phyllotaxis, root-rectangles (√1–√5), reciprocal diagonals, and whirling squares.

hambidge:1920-vase.author: Jay Hambidge
hambidge:1920-vase.locus: Chs. I–III (Static vs. Dynamic Symmetry, Phyllotaxis, Root-Five & Whirling-Square Rectangles)
hambidge:1920-vase.publisher: Yale University Press, New Haven & New York
hambidge:1920-vase.note: Connects biological growth laws (shells and phyllotaxis) directly to Greek commensurability in square (Euclid Book X) and classical harmonic design.

heath:1908.author: Sir Thomas Little Heath
heath:1908.work: The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements, Translated from the Text of Heiberg with Introduction and Commentary
heath:1908.locus: Vol. I (Book II Def. 2, pp. 370–372); Vol. II (Book IV.10, VI.30); Vol. III (Books X & XIII)
heath:1908.note: Standard Cambridge philological commentary cited alongside Thompson's historical reconstruction of Greek gnomonic geometry.

hero:def.author: Hero of Alexandria
hero:def.work: Definitiones (Heronis Alexandrini Opera quae supersunt omnia, Vol. IV, ed. J. L. Heiberg)
hero:def.note: Preserves the generalized Greek definition of a gnomon as any increment leaving a figure geometrically similar to itself (Ch. XI, p. 509).

hofmeister:1868.author: Wilhelm Hofmeister
hofmeister:1868.locus: Handbuch der physiologischen Botanik, Bd. I, Abt. 2
hofmeister:1868.note: Formulates Hofmeister's mechanical gap-rule for leaf primordia at the growing apex (Ch. XIV, pp. 648–651).

kelvin:1887.author: Sir William Thomson (Lord Kelvin)
kelvin:1887.work: On the Division of Space with Minimum Partitional Area
kelvin:1887.locus: Philosophical Magazine, 5th series, Vol. 24, No. 151, pp. 503–514
kelvin:1887.note: Demonstrates the minimal-foam space partition by 14-hedra (tetrakaidecahedra: 8 hexagons and 6 squares), applied to cellular parenchyma in Chapters VII–VIII (pp. 338–345).

kepler:1611.author: Johannes Kepler
kepler:1611.work: Strena seu De Nive Sexangula (The Six-Cornered Snowflake)
kepler:1611.locus: On Bee Cells, Pomegranate Packing & the Rhombic Dodecahedron
kepler:1611.note: First geometric description of the space-filling rhombic dodecahedron formed by close-packed spheres and opposed honeycomb layers (Ch. VII, pp. 328–336).

maclaurin:1743.author: Colin Maclaurin
maclaurin:1743.work: Of the Bases of the Cells wherein the Bees deposite their Honey
maclaurin:1743.locus: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society, Vol. 42, No. 471, pp. 565–571
maclaurin:1743.note: Proves purely by Euclidean geometry that the minimum-surface rhombic cap has obtuse angle 2 arctan(√2) = 109° 28′ 16″ (Ch. VII, p. 332).

maraldi:1712.author: Giacomo Filippo Maraldi
maraldi:1712.locus: Histoire et Mémoires de l'Académie Royale des Sciences (année 1712), pp. 299–335
maraldi:1712.note: Empirical measurement of the rhombic inclination and obtuse dihedral/planar angles (~109° 28′ and 70° 32′) of the honeybee's cell (Ch. VII, pp. 329–334).

meyer:1867.author: Georg Hermann von Meyer
meyer:1867.locus: Archiv für Anatomie, Physiologie und wissenschaftliche Medicin (Reicherts und Du Bois-Reymonds Archiv), pp. 615–628
meyer:1867.note: Reveals the regular curved trajectories of cancellous bone trabeculae in the human femur and calcaneus, paired with Culmann's crane diagram (Ch. XVI, pp. 679–686).

moseley:1838.author: Henry Moseley
moseley:1838.work: On the Geometrical Forms of Turbinated and Discoid Shells
moseley:1838.locus: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London, Vol. 128, pp. 351–370
moseley:1838.note: Classic analytical study of logarithmic spiral shells and opercula upon which Chapter XI of On Growth and Form builds directly.

pacioli:1509.author: Fra Luca Pacioli
pacioli:1509.work: De Divina Proportione (illustrations by Leonardo da Vinci)
pacioli:1509.locus: Pars Prima (Divine Proportion φ & Platonic Polyhedra)
pacioli:1509.note: Renaissance treatise on extreme and mean ratio and regular polyhedra, bridged in GEOMETOR to Thompson's gnomons and radiolarian polyhedra.

pappus:synagoge.author: Pappus of Alexandria
pappus:synagoge.locus: Book V Preface (On the Sagacity of Bees & Isoperimetry); Book VII (Domain of Analysis & Cross-Ratio)
pappus:synagoge.note: Unites the classical isoperimetric proof of the hexagonal honeycomb (Ch. VII, p. 327) with the projective cross-ratio transformations underlying Chapter XVII.

plateau:1873.author: Joseph Antoine Ferdinand Plateau
plateau:1873.work: Statique expérimentale et théorique des liquides soumis aux seules forces moléculaires
plateau:1873.note: Definitive treatise on soap films, minimal surfaces, Delaunay surfaces of constant mean curvature, and cellular foam equilibria (Chs. V–IX).

tait:1872.author: Peter Guthrie Tait
tait:1872.locus: Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh, Vol. 7, pp. 391–394
tait:1872.note: Demonstrates geometrically how overlapping cylindrical parastichy lattices generate Fibonacci recurrence numbers (Ch. XIV, pp. 643–645, Fig. 325).

thompson:1911.author: D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson
thompson:1911.work: Magnalia Naturae; or, The Greater Problems of Biology
thompson:1911.locus: Presidential Address to Section D (Zoology), British Association for the Advancement of Science, Portsmouth (also Science, Vol. 34, pp. 417–428)
thompson:1911.note: Programmatic address introducing the Aquinas epigraph and calling for physical and mathematical morphology prior to On Growth and Form.

thompson:1915.author: D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson
thompson:1915.locus: Transactions of the Royal Society of Edinburgh, Vol. 50, Part IV, No. 27, pp. 857–895
thompson:1915.note: First publication of Thompson's coordinate transformation grids (Argyropelecus/Sternoptyx, Diodon/Orthagoriscus, crab carapaces, Eohippus/Equus), expanded into Chapter XVII of the 1917 edition.

thompson:1917.author: D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson
thompson:1917.note: Authoritative 1917 First Edition reproduced in this Digital Scriptorium Book Codex.

turing:1952.author: Alan Mathison Turing
turing:1952.locus: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London, Series B, Vol. 237, No. 641, pp. 37–72
turing:1952.note: Foundational reaction-diffusion paper explicitly citing Thompson's On Growth and Form as inspiration for mathematical morphogenesis and phyllotaxis.
